clue.text: Damage shoreline heartlessly

indicators.note: without a heart, so the central letter of the shoreline word is removed

parts.note: a coast is a shoreline

explanation.surface: Something, perhaps a storm, has harmed the shoreline without pity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' takes the middle A out of COAST. 'Damage' is the informal price, as in 'what's the damage?'
explanation.definitionFit: In informal speech the damage is the price or bill you must pay.

clue.text: Quality raised in top hospital monument

indicators.note: the raised piece is placed in the top word

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: tone is a quality, as of sound
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A fine memorial is put up on top of a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TONE into ENOT, set 'in' CAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a war memorial honouring those buried elsewhere.

clue.text: Polish students upset, with 25% of students supporting light explosion

indicators.note: in a down clue, the supporting piece sits below
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: to rub is to polish
NUS is the National Union of Students

indicators.note: a quarter of the word students, its first two letters

explanation.surface: Students in Poland are upset, with some of them backing a burst of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses RUB + NUS to SUNBUR; '25% of' takes ST, two of the eight letters of students, which goes below ('supporting').
explanation.definitionFit: A sunburst is sudden sunshine breaking through clouds, an explosion of light.

clue.text: Feasible American soldiers will occupy lakes and part of US

indicators.note: to occupy is to sit inside, so these letters go within the lakes pair

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake, doubled for the plural
on means feasible, as in 'that's not on'
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: A plan to station US troops by some lakes is judged workable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will occupy' signals insertion between the two lake letters. 'Feasible' as ON is the sense in 'that's not on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Long Island is a large island belonging to New York State, so a region of the United States.

clue.text: No longer too young to work hard in Rome (odd parts excepted)

indicators.note: the hard-work word goes in the letters kept from Rome
the odd-numbered letters are excluded, so only the even ones remain

parts.note: to fag is to toil, a British informal sense

explanation.surface: An adult finally allowed to labour in Rome, with some exceptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd parts excepted' keeps Rome's second and fourth letters, OE, and 'in' signals insertion. To fag is British slang for toiling, as public-school juniors once did for seniors.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of age means having reached adulthood, so no longer a minor.

clue.text: Become aware of, say, rising energy in dance leading to love

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: e.g. means say, for example

indicators.note: the energy letter is put in the dance

parts.note: the twist is a 1960s dance
E is the physics symbol for energy
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone notices, say, a surge of energy in a dance that leads to romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' makes GE; 'in' puts E into TWIST to give TWISET.
explanation.definitionFit: To get wise to something is to realise or discover it, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Islanders certainly upset about welcome provided by island

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means overturned, so read backwards

parts.note: yes means certainly
C is circa, about
hello is a welcome

explanation.surface: Islanders are certainly upset about the greeting an island gives them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns YES into SEY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seychellois are the people of the Seychelles, an Indian Ocean archipelago nation.

clue.text: A graduate securing second degree ultimately is simple creature

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the A-and-graduate pair holds the others inside

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A graduate getting a further degree is, in the end, a simple soul.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoeba is a single-celled organism, about the simplest form of life.

clue.text: Old plane satisfactory in a little soaring

indicators.note: in a down clue, soaring means going upwards, so read backwards
the satisfactory letters are placed in the little word

parts.note: a tad is a little
OK means satisfactory

explanation.surface: An old aircraft climbs a little, and that's fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives ATOKAD, and 'soaring' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Douglas Dakota was a Second World War transport aircraft, now vintage.

clue.text: Fashionable, residing in last section of Sloane Square

indicators.note: something residing in a place lives within it, so these letters go inside
only the closing stretch of the word Sloane is kept, its opening letters dropped

parts.note: Sloane is taken as written before its front is cut away
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: A trendy person lives at the far end of a smart London square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last section of' takes NE from Sloane, and 'residing in' puts IN inside it. Sloane Square is a smart London square; 'Square' is really the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is three times three, a square number.

clue.text: Old man's attempt to manipulate baker

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, the old man, with the possessive S
a try is an attempt
to cook the books is to manipulate them

explanation.surface: Dad tries to fiddle the accounts of a baker.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastrycook makes pastries and cakes, so works as a baker.

clue.text: Source of this disorder is fungus

indicators.note: the source is the beginning, so the first letter of this is taken

parts.note: to ruffle is to disorder, as hair

explanation.surface: A fungus is blamed as the cause of some illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A truffle is an edible underground fungus prized by cooks.

clue.text: 'Attractive and how French?' It's a reasonable thing to say

parts.note: fair means attractive, as in fair maiden
comment is the French word for how

explanation.surface: A quoted question asks whether something is attractive, and how, in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair comment is an idiom for a justified remark that nobody can reasonably object to.

clue.text: People soon surrounding husband

indicators.note: the soon phrase surrounds, so the husband letter goes inside it

parts.note: in a bit means soon

explanation.surface: Folk will shortly gather round a married man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People' is a verb here: to people a place is to live in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To people a land is to fill it with inhabitants, that is, to occupy it.

clue.text: Record of death: two sons being laid out in shroud

indicators.note: these letters are placed in the shroud word

parts.note: a pall is a cloth shroud over a coffin
S is the abbreviation for son, doubled

indicators.note: laying out arranges things anew, so the letters of being are reordered

explanation.surface: A death is recorded as two sons are laid out in burial cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid out' shuffles being to INGBE and 'in' signals insertion into the shroud; 'laid out' also suits the funeral picture, hiding the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A passing bell is tolled to announce someone has died, a public notice of the death.

clue.text: House style, say, covering variant spelling of i.e. 'dueling'

indicators.note: a different spelling rearranges the letters given

explanation.surface: A publisher's style guide addresses the American spelling of duelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks house style as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A house style is one example of a guideline, a rule a publisher's writers follow.

clue.text: Liqueur couple found around club in Pacific country

parts.note: kir is a drink of white wine with blackcurrant liqueur

indicators.note: the couple letters are found surrounding the club

parts.note: II is the Roman numeral two
a bat is a club

explanation.surface: A pair discover a drink near a Pacific nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiribati is an island republic in the central Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Stout, conceivably excellent example

parts.note: the word stout can be seen as ST joined to OUT, so the answer read as an instruction builds it

explanation.surface: Stout, you might think, is a fine example of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as wordplay, is ST and OUT, which put together spell stout.
explanation.definitionFit: A standout is something that is outstanding, the best example of its kind.

clue.text: 'Hip doctor' is wrong here

indicators.note: letters set wrong are rearranged, so the phrase is shuffled

explanation.surface: Calling this specialist a hip doctor would be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' shuffles HIPDOCTORIS. The whole clue also defines: this doctor works on feet, far below the hip.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiropodist treats feet, so calling one a hip doctor is wrong.

clue.text: A banking system enshrining universal approach to counting

indicators.note: to enshrine is to hold within, so the universal letter goes inside

parts.note: BACS is the UK electronic bank payment system
U is the British film rating meaning universal

explanation.surface: A bank's system includes a universal method of counting money.
explanation.walkthrough: BACS is the British automated bank payment system.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads used for counting, an approach to arithmetic.

clue.text: Useless dossier — just regularly missing inside

indicators.note: the kept letters go inside the dossier word

parts.note: a file is a dossier

indicators.note: every other letter is dropped from just, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: A worthless file, with just a few bits gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly missing' drops J and S from just, leaving UT.
explanation.definitionFit: Futile means pointless or ineffective, achieving nothing.

clue.text: Bishop meeting stranger, spurning last city resident

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: to spurn the last is to reject the final letter

parts.note: rummier means stranger, from rum meaning odd

explanation.surface: A cleric meets an odd newcomer who shuns the final one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spurning last' drops the closing R from RUMMIER. A Brummie is someone from Birmingham, England's second city.
explanation.definitionFit: Brummie is the informal name for an inhabitant of Birmingham.

clue.text: Copper quietly willing to nab one buffer

indicators.note: to nab is to seize and hold, so the one letter is held inside

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
sh is a call for quiet
on means willing, as in 'I'm on for it'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A policeman, keen to catch someone discreetly, does so softly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is the metal, not a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushion softens a blow, acting as a buffer.

clue.text: Run and run in pursuit of tea

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the run letter comes after

parts.note: chai is tea
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone runs and runs to chase a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To chair a meeting is to run or preside over it.

clue.text: Minister's seeing student replaced by that man of fanciful views

indicators.note: one piece swapped out for another signals substitution

parts.note: clerical means belonging to a minister of religion
L is the learner abbreviation, a student
him is the pronoun for that man

explanation.surface: A minister's student is swapped for a dreamer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced by' swaps the L in CLERICAL for HIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimerical means wildly imaginary, like the mythical chimera, so holding unrealistic notions.

clue.text: Exclamation of surprise with one of the lines overlooked in part of religious picture

indicators.note: something overlooked is left out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: hallo is a cry of surprise
L is an abbreviation for line, and hallo holds two of them

explanation.surface: Someone gasps at an altarpiece where one stroke of paint was missed.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is the ring of light painted around a saint's head in religious art.

clue.text: Steady weather set to turn stormy

indicators.note: weather turning stormy is thrown into turmoil, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A forecast: settled weather is about to become wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steady' is a noun, a regular boyfriend or girlfriend, not a description of the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady is someone you are going out with regularly, a romantic partner.

clue.text: What droplets are, nothing less!

indicators.note: less means without, so the letter for nothing is removed

parts.note: droplets are moist, being wet
O is the zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An exclamation insisting droplets are exactly that and no less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' takes O out of MOIST. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer, which is made of fine droplets.
explanation.definitionFit: Mist is a haze of tiny water droplets suspended in the air.
